description: Write the incoming 3D solids to a mesh file (glTF / OBJ / STL / PLY) and download it — the 3D twin of Export DXF. Wire a 3D Render node in and every row it built is exported.
instructions:
A SINK: wire any 3D geometry into its input and press Download. Nothing is added to the scene and nothing is committed — the node only writes the file.

WIRE A 3D RENDER NODE IN and every solid its rows built is exported, exactly as the viewport shows it: Cuboid and Cylinder rows with their dimensions and per-point placements, Polyhedron rows with their computed face lists. A single 3D primitive (Cuboid, Cylinder, Sphere, Frustum …) with its Transform 3D chain exports the same way.

FORMAT decides what survives:
• glTF (.glb) — geometry AND colour, one self-contained binary. The default, and what to use for Blender / three.js / AR.
• Wavefront (.obj) — geometry only (three's OBJ writer emits no material file), but the most widely accepted CAD interchange.
• STL (.stl) — triangles only, no colour: 3D printing.
• PLY (.ply) — geometry with per-vertex colour.

AXIS: the viewport is Y-up. "Z up" rotates the export so Z is up and +Y is north — the convention CAD and Blender expect, and the one the DXF export writes, so a 2D and a 3D export of the same object line up. Choose "Y up" only for a glTF/three.js pipeline that expects the raw scene frame.

UNITS scale the metre coordinates on the way out.
